records.c: Twenty consecutive 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank $4000. Each slot begins with 21 rows of three pixel bytes, and the last byte is outside the displayed height.
Four sprite slots after the first sixteen mission frames. The VIC slot positions relative to bank $4000 are $A0-$A3.

Four rows of four character codes per 16-byte tile. The map renderer resolves a tile ID through the resident screen-code pointer tables, then indexes this pattern with the character coordinates modulo four.
Tile IDs $40-$50 use the upper end of the populated dictionary. Each row is four character indices wide, starting at $C400 for ID $40.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $51–$90. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $91–$AF. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Complete 256-glyph source for the $ADF7 scene. Each glyph occupies eight bytes. The masked wipe at $1E17 reads from this base with an eight-byte stride and writes the corresponding row at $4000.
Tile-indexed colour bytes. The initial playfield renderer at $17CD reads these in parallel with the tile character pointers and $1882 writes the chosen value to colour RAM.
Primary 256-character graphics source. The resident wipe routine at $1DC2 enables RAM under I/O and copies the selected pixel rows to the live character set at $4000.
Rows for character codes $80-$FF in the main stage's 256-glyph set. The masked copy selects them through the same eight-byte stride as the lower codes.
Alternate 256-character graphics source in RAM below the I/O window. The resident wipe routine chooses this source when $1902 is set, unless the alternate scene flag $ADF7 takes priority.
The upper half of the alternate stage's eight-byte character slots, read under CIA and expansion register addresses with I/O banked out.
Stage 1 grid, 60 entries per row and first 8 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 1 tile grid from row 9, column 1. The grid has 60 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Final 36 bytes of a 96-byte copy of the playfield glyph bytes at $D1E1–$D240. This part of the copy lies past the declared stage-one tile grid.
The tile allocation resumes a run of 192 values from zero through seven after the copied glyph bytes. They follow the nine rows declared by the stage-one descriptor.
Stage 1 grid, 60 entries per row and first 8 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 1 attribute grid from row 9, column 1. The grid has 60 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Two extra 60-cell attribute rows follow the declared stage-one grid. Both repeat the preceding row, with bit one set in the sixteenth column and all other cells zero.
Zero fill between the retained stage-one attribute rows and the stage-two tile grid.
Stage 2 grid, 60 entries per row and first 8 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 2 tile grid from row 9, column 1. The grid has 60 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 2 grid, 60 entries per row and first 8 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 attribute grid from row 9, column 1. The grid has 60 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
One extra 60-cell row follows the declared stage-two attribute grid. Cell 22 holds $66, whose low bits are six and whose placement type field is twelve. The other cells in the row are zero.
Zero fill between the retained attribute row and the stage-three tile grid.
Stage 3 grid, 10 entries per row and first 6 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 3 tile grid from row 7, column 1. The grid has 10 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
The declared stage-three tile grid is followed by 58 copies of tile $44 before the attribute grid.
Stage 3 grid, 10 entries per row and first 6 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 3 attribute grid from row 7, column 1. The grid has 10 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Loaded zero bytes following the seven declared rows of the stage-three attribute grid.

Twelve rows of forty character indices. The panel update selects an eleven-column window starting at the offset in $C8 and reads its rows through the table at $EE00. A space leaves the visible layer's existing cell in place.
Row 2 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 3 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 4 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 5 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 6 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 7 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 8 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 9 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 10 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 11 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
Row 12 of the panel. The row pointer table at $EE00 selects its 40 character indices, and the renderer draws an eleven-column window.
The panel allocation ends with 32 copies of character index $99 before its split row pointers at $EE00.
Split row addresses, low bytes at $EE00 and high bytes at $EE10, spaced 40 bytes apart. The loop at $EE91 reads entries zero through eleven for the panel window.
Second half of the panel's 16 low address bytes. The panel loop reads entries eight through eleven here for its final four rows.
High bytes of the panel row addresses, paired with the low bytes at $EE00. The renderer loads each pair at $EE91.
When nonzero the panel update decrements this counter and starts the source window at column 12 instead of 1.
When nonzero the panel update decrements this counter, shifts the source window one column left and uses colour 9 instead of 8.
Incremented with both window counters at zero. The idle update draws only when the low two bits are clear.
Reads $31. For values 1 or 2 sets $2C to 1 and clears $27. Clears $31 on those paths and leaves zero unchanged and subtracts two from values above 2.
Stores the stage-complete result in $2C, clears the contact outcome and writes the remaining count to $31.

Selects a source column and colour from the countdowns. Draws twelve rows of eleven cells at $4908, taking non-space characters from the panel table or copying the corresponding $4D08 screen cell at a space. Writes matching colour RAM at $D908. Increments all three destination addresses by 40 per row.
Uses the idle divider and two countdowns to choose whether to redraw. Patches the colour and window origin before rebuilding the row addresses.
Writes the selected character to the patched front screen address plus the column in X.
Low byte of the patched front screen address for this panel row.
High byte of the patched destination. For a space in the panel source, the other branch loads the background character from the alternate screen and rejoins the store.
Low byte of the alternate screen row in the load at $EEAE.
High byte of the alternate screen row. The load returns to the same front screen store used for opaque panel characters.
Immediate colour value eight in the load at $EEB4.
Writes eight to the panel cell's patched colour RAM address.
Low byte of the colour RAM row address.
High byte of the colour RAM row address. Advances the destination and source columns until eleven characters have been drawn.
Adds 40 to the three operands used for front screen, alternate screen and colour RAM, including carry into each high byte. Repeats until the twelfth row.
Sixteen low-byte components used with the parallel whole-byte table at $EF0B when the actor changes X.
Whole-byte X components paired with the low bytes at $EEFA. The movement handler applies addition or subtraction according to the direction flags.
Sixteen direction-indexed values. A zero entry skips the X step in the actor movement loop.
Sixteen direction-indexed step values subtracted from or added to $0BF7 before the Y update at $0BD0.
Whole-byte Y components used by $EF60 alongside the table at $EF2D.
Selects the sign of the $0BD0 and $0BF7 updates for the current direction.
Advances the actor using the direction tables at $EEFA–$EF5E and turns it at the X and Y limits. Refreshes its turn step from the four-entry table at $F043 and chooses frame $80 or $81.
Four possible increments to the actor direction, alternating +1 and -1.
Current and recent low X positions used by the sprite compositor at $F139.
High X positions accompanying the low X data and used to set the sprite's ninth hardware X bit.
Current and recent Y positions read by the sprite compositor.
Slot number supplied to the compositor at $F139.
Circulating history counter masked to three bits for each actor's history slots.

Clears the high sprite X bits for the upper four slots. Skips the first slot when its Y is zero and updates the second slot without that check. Displays one history position, saves the current position back to the ring and writes the four sprites' frame pointers and colours.

Immediate sprite phase at $F0B5, toggled by XOR with four. The low three bits choose a position from the eight-entry group for the current actor. The same phase chooses the pointer for sprites six and seven before the update sets the pair colours.
Writes the X and Y bytes of the selected history slot to the selected VIC sprite and sets the X high bit when the history's high byte is nonzero.
Immediate X-high bit mask for the VIC register at $D010. The writer patches it from the sprite's bit in the table at $2965.
Immediate LDX operand at $F15E. The sprite writer saves its input X here at $F139.
Decremented in the alternate update and reset to 100 on spawn or a successful target shot.
Alternates between actor slots 0 and 1 when the spawn timer expires.

Updates the panel and sprites and checks player and shot overlap. On timer expiry, alternates the active actor slot, assigns its first position and direction, starts the panel countdown and triggers effect 7.
Checks both active alternate-stage actors when $27 is clear. Compares wrapped X separation and a Y window using one of two player Y bases. On overlap sets $27 and writes $17 to $0C4D.
Immediate threshold for the preceding comparison, patched by the player pose check. The following branches accept near vertical overlap and set outcome one with a cooldown of $17.
Checks both live shot slots for tile row 6 or 7 and column $1B. A match sets the panel adjustment countdown, stops the shot, restarts the spawn timer and decrements $31. On zero sets $2C to 1.
Two loaded bytes, $C5 and $60, immediately after the return at $F261 and before the zero fill.
Loaded zero fill following the alternate-stage routines, ending before the isolated value at $F32F.
Screen code $66 at column 48 of the fifth 64-byte source row under $F200. With horizontal origin $EC, the load at $F862 selects this cell for screen column 28.

Twenty-six zero screen codes spanning the end of secondary-scene row four and the start of row five, counting from zero. With source row five and origin $10, the renderer at $F862 read the last zero at $F349.
Screen code $91 at column 11 of the sixth source row. With horizontal origin $10, the renderer selects it for screen column 27.
Zero screen codes from $F34B through $F4D4 in the 64-column secondary scene. A controlled draw of row five with origin $10 read the first zero at $F34B through $F862.
Screen code $21 at column 22 of the twelfth source row. With horizontal origin $10, the renderer selects it for screen column 38.
Loaded zero fill from the byte after $F4D5 through the page before $F800.
Screen row index passed through memory to $F808.
Seven initial bytes after the renderer's row index. The final six form the sequence 0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, matching the suffix of the Mission 2 row workspace at $F80B–$F810.

Clears 40 characters in the selected screen row when the row index at $F800 is below 16. Uses the difference from $9423 as a 64-byte row index under $F200, and starts writing at the column in $9422. In this overlay the source overlaps the active stage code.
Fine scroll offsets for X and Y. The fine handler updates one axis and copies its scaled value to the display workspace.
Six bytes after the two fine-scroll positions. The direction-to-axis map at $F9AA selects zero or one for the reads and writes based at $F86E. The suffix is $00,$00,$0F,$00,$0F,$00.
Counts the rendered rows, and gates the page flip until it reaches 16.

Initializes a separate set of image origins and motion counters at $9420 when $21CE is clear. Draws pending rows through $F808, advances the scene and its actors, and picks an accent colour. If $9427 is set, branches to the exit sequence.

Disables sprites, sets up the fine scroll and redraws the selected screen page. Waits twice on $1C5E, switches pages and adjusts the scene origins. At the exit thresholds, sets $1C5F and writes $0B to $941F.
The scene update decrements this value and uses bits 2–4 as the accent palette index.
Eight colours selected by the accent counter. The painter receives the selected value with bit three set.
Four signed scroll increments, with minus one followed by plus one for each axis.
Four fine scroll endpoints, $0F and zero for each axis.
A second set of the four alternating $0F and zero fine-scroll limits. The direction is masked to two bits at $FA04, so the comparisons based at $F9A2 use the first set.
Maps the first two directions to X and the second two to Y.

Checks the current direction and fine limit before starting another coarse shift. Picks one of four directions when the count expires, adjusts the requested origin by one, and resets the row renderer.

Moves the active axis modulo 16. At the endpoint restores the preceding fine position until all 16 rows are ready, then commits the coarse origin and swaps screen pages. Writes the halved fine position with bit four set for the display.
Zero byte between the fine scroll return and the four origin limits at $FA5F.
Four coordinate limits that cause the coarse scheduler to choose another direction.
Seven bytes between the four origin limits and the accent painter's offsets. The limit comparison at $F9E7 uses the direction in X, selected with the two-bit mask at $FA04.
Sixteen offsets in four successive screen rows. The accent painter uses them to address a four-by-four group of colour cells.
Builds the colour RAM base from the coarse origins, then writes the accent in $FA at sixteen offsets and applies the edge colour at four successive row starts. Restores X and Y.
Returns eight times the coarse Y origin plus $13, where the addition precedes the scaling.
Stores eight times the coarse X origin plus $15 in $CA/$CB, where the addition precedes the scaling.

Clears three activity bytes and sets $2AA7 to two. When the coarse vertical origin passes the threshold, the delay expires and a slot is clear, prepares screen-relative coordinates and calls $8CC2 with type eleven.
Spawn delay decremented while the coarse vertical index permits actors.

Checks two active shots against screen cells. A non-space cell clears the shot. Colour $0A triggers the accent and decrements $A9E9. Its last hit sets the exit flag and copies the active origins to the requested origins.
The two Y positions stored in the sprite registers by $FC4F.
One Y limit per sprite. The movement loop compares each nonzero position to its limit before adding three.
Spawn delay counted down at $FBB5 and reset to $96 after starting the pair.
Waits for the spawn delay, a clear first actor slot and an inactive pair. Seeds X and both Y positions from the coarse origin, then sets the active flag and reloads the delay.

Moves the active pair left two units and retires it when X falls below ten. Updates the two sprites' X high bits, moves each Y toward its bound, and writes both screens' pointers from the shared animation counter.
Requires an active sprite pair and a wrapped half-resolution X difference within the contact window. With player Y at least $7A, writes the contact flag and a delay of $17.

Partial second copy of the neighbouring sprite-pair contact test. It retains the half-resolution horizontal comparisons and begins the vertical check. The return and the forward branch destination lie beyond the start of mission metadata.
The one-based mission number used for this file and for play selection in the resident engine.
Four split pointers with their high bytes at $FCC5. The resident loader at $0B26 selects a stage and gives its grid to the row-pointer builder at $0B46.
High bytes for the tile grids. $0B2B takes the entry for the active stage and puts it in $FC before generating row pointers.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCCD. The grid parallels the tile map and the resident coordinate lookup at $3DFA masks each attribute to its low three bits.
High bytes for the attribute grids. $0B35 selects the high byte for $FE.
Stage widths used as a byte stride for the tile and attribute row pointers.
Stage heights used by the resident scaler to derive the vertical playfield limit and by $8EAD to walk the attribute grid.
Indexed stage values copied to $2D during setup by $0AFD.
VIC extended background register $D022 values selected by stage.
VIC extended background register $D023 values selected by stage.
Indexed initial view value written to $1781 before the character drawing loop at $1785.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCED. $8FE8 copies 128 bytes from the selected source into a separate workspace half for each player.
High bytes for the placement seeds. $8FF3 selects one for $FC before copying seeds to player workspace.
Indexed stage bytes cached at $0AEA and $0BE0 before display setup.
Stage index compared at $1A82. A match enables the alternate source at $D800 and installs the two operand bytes following this value at $1642/$1643.
Low and high bytes written to $1642/$1643 on the stage selected by $FCF5.
High byte of the target address for the alternate stage callback patched at $1642/$1643.
Four stage-indexed masks copied to $1901 at $0B11. The resident sprite routines AND their priority bits with this mask before writing VIC register $D01B.
The pair at $FCFC/$FCFD supplies the two operand bytes at $2B0A/$2B0B.
High byte of the pair installed at $2B0A/$2B0B.
Low and high bytes of the mission-provided routine that $1AB3 calls after preparing the stage grids.
High byte of the stage setup call target, installed at $1AB5.

Sixteen triplets in the address-low, address-high and value format of the stage placement records. All destinations fall in the stage one attribute area. The stage placement directory selects $FD80 or $FE00.

A copy of the sixteen default C64 KERNAL RAM vectors at $0314–$0333. The entries begin with the IRQ, BRK and NMI targets $EA31, $FE66 and $FE47, followed by the BASIC and device I/O hooks. All five mission payloads carry the same copy.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the shared bytes at $FD30 and the stage placement source at $FD80.

Stage 1 placement seed copied into player workspace by $8FE8. A record has a destination low byte, destination high byte and value. A zero value ends the loop that applies records to the working stage grid.
Stage 2 placement seed copied into page $0200. The resident setup applies the value of each record at its two-byte destination and stops at the first zero value.
The final 112 bytes of the loaded mission stream are zero. Mission 1's stage placement pointers select $FD80 or $FE00.
